name: British fascism
summary: British fascism is the family of ultranationalist, authoritarian movements of interwar and later Britain, above all Oswald Mosley's British Union of Fascists. It wanted to replace parliamentary party politics with a strong leader and a corporate state in which employers, workers and finance are organised by industry under state authority, with protection and an economically self-contained nation and Empire. It promised national rebirth, hostility to Communism and alien finance, and opposed immigration and race-mixing, with antisemitism growing in the BUF and central to Leese's Imperial Fascist League.
scope: The mainstream of the British Union of Fascists under Mosley in its peak years (1932-1940), based on The Greater Britain (1932) and scholarly accounts. Leese's Imperial Fascist League is noted as a more Nazi-aligned, openly racial strand. Postwar Union Movement, National Front and BNP are treated as later heirs and excluded except where noted.

sources.title: National Front (United Kingdom)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Postwar heirs' stance on immigration, repatriation, eugenics, gender and capital punishment; used only for low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Mosley's programme stressed state-organised production and purchasing power but the sources opened do not describe a health service, so this is inferred and left neutral.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The corporate system was to fix wages through permanent machinery and raise purchasing power, which implies state-set wage floors rather than a market wage.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mosley rejected laissez-faire and wanted the state to direct rationalised industry, though profit and enterprise were kept within national limits.

public-ownership.rationale: He rejected Whitehall socialism for the self-government of industry in corporations; industries stayed privately owned under state authority.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The opened sources give no tax programme; the movement attacked alien finance rather than the wealthy as such, so no clear answer can be inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Unions were to be folded into the state's corporate machinery and denied independent class-struggle roles, so independent unions are not praised.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property and profit were kept but all within the state and subject to national limits ("none outside the State"), so it is not a near-absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Industry and finance were to sit under state authority, with finance made the handmaid of industry, which means tighter regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Mosley's economics aimed to raise consumption and employment, but the sources describe no detailed welfare policy; inferred disagreement from his stress on purchasing power.

worker-ownership.rationale: He rejected socialism; workers and employers were to cooperate in state-supervised corporations, not workers owning firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed directly; a movement demanding strong executive government and security against communism would likely accept it, but this is an inference.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the disciplined, obligation-centred public ethic Mosley preached.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The BUF was itself targeted by public order law and claimed free speech for itself, so restrictions on hate speech were opposed, though it would not extend this to opponents.

strong-leader.rationale: Mosley wanted strong executive government and equated Dictatorship with Leadership, bypassing a Parliament of obstruction and talk.

state-harmful.rationale: The corporate state placed everything "within the State; none outside the State; none against the State."

limit-guns.rationale: No source opened addresses gun policy; adherents emphasised order and state power but also paramilitary self-defence stewards.

empower-police-military.rationale: The movement was militarist, favoured order and state authority and defended the empire by force, though the BUF clashed with police over public order.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from opposition to homosexuality and the moral-renewal and discipline themes.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the discipline, obligation and national-duty ethic.

traditional-family.rationale: Women were to be educated to serve family and nation and men to be breadwinners, although the BUF also courted women with maternity support.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Homosexuality was opposed and gender roles emphasised virility, so same-sex marriage would be firmly rejected (an anachronistic but clear inference).

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion is not covered for the BUF; the later National Front opposed it, and a pro-natal, family-centred outlook points the same way.

more-religion-public.rationale: The BUF opposed atheism and sought closer church-state links while professing toleration, and Mosley said Fascism should fit with religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racialist views were common, and Mosley opposed race-mixing and immigration, so remedial policies for racial groups would be rejected.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Movements promoted a virile masculinity and distinct sex roles ("men who are men and women who are women"), the opposite of a social-construct view.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: British fascism combined ultranationalism with claims to English tradition and the slogan "Britain for the British".

gradual-change.rationale: Mosley presented Fascism as a break with a failed parliamentary system, requiring will and a new state rather than gradual reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mosley opposed immigration under "Britain for the British", and he called alien labour a menace to the white standard of life.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He rejected international agreements and the League as a route to recovery in favour of national measures and an Empire self-contained.

free-trade.rationale: The programme was protection and autarchy of nation and Empire, with exclusion of foreign food and conditional tariffs.

nation-first.rationale: Autarchy for the nation and Empire and rejection of international solutions, and later non-interventionism, put Britain first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The BUF practised selective pacifism, opposing wars not defending Britain or the Empire, so intervention for others' rights would be rejected.

open-borders.rationale: Opposed immigration and mixing under "Britain for the British", with borders firmly closed.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; Mosley sought expansion of production and consumption through a rationalised state, though a self-contained economy is not growth-limiting by design.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no relevant position, and the corporatist state would act drastically but no environmental concern is documented.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Mosley saw rationalised industry as inevitable and thought the rationalised state could master its effects, a technocratic modernism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the modernist, state-directed industrial and autarkic outlook that favours domestic energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: The BUF aimed to take power via the existing political order while using paramilitary mobilisation; Mosley said voters could still remove governments, so adherents are split on revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: The occupational franchise was justified as a government of experts elected by experts, with a specialist chamber replacing the Lords.

central-planning.rationale: Mosley wanted state direction of rationalised industry and planned autarky but kept private enterprise and rejected Whitehall socialism, so full central planning is not endorsed.

socialized-markets.rationale: The question presupposes socialist ownership; the BUF rejected socialism but did envisage markets within corporate limits, so mild disagreement.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not part of the programme in the sources opened; inferred disagreement.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No stated position in the opened sources.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; the ethos of obligation and corporate wage-setting points against an unconditional payment.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protection was central, though conditional on wages and prices: "Protection must protect organisation, and not chaos."

state-directs-investment.rationale: Mosley wanted British finance directed to equip British industry and the state to guide rationalised industry.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mosley defended agriculture and enterprise but also rationalised large industry; no clear small-owner programme in the sources opened.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wages and profit remained, regulated by corporate machinery; abolition is opposed as Marxist.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Mosley wanted finance subordinated to the state and industry, not left to the market, which is opposite to the premise.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Employers and workers organised in state-supervised corporations regulating wages and prices through permanent machinery, the core of the programme.

one-party-rule.rationale: Adherents wanted fascist rule on the Italian or German model, but Mosley qualified it by saying voters could remove governments, so it is not a strong yes.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The BUF professed absolute loyalty to the Crown and said Fascism would strengthen it, though the Leese strand was more sceptical.

democracy-best.rationale: Mosley said the parliamentary system was the negation of the people's will and replaced it with corporate leadership.

direct-votes.rationale: The scheme was an occupational franchise and strong executive, not referendums on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Corporations under state authority replaced parliaments, but as state bodies and not councils of workers holding power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Ultranationalist and imperial unity; the BUF extended corporatism across the Empire and opposed fragmentation.

natural-rulers.rationale: Leadership by a dictator-leader, an expert specialist chamber and the Leese strand's aristocratic order imply some are born to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Blackshirt stewards fought opponents, and the movement saw force as necessary: "We have the Power, but Fascism alone has the Will."

war-builds-character.rationale: Joyce and Leese held war and imperialism the ultimate expression of national identity, but the BUF's selective pacifism makes the mainstream answer a mild yes.

separate-church-state.rationale: The BUF sought a closer link between church and state while professing toleration.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Closer church-state ties were desired but not scriptural law; Mosley said Fascism should fit with religion.

private-courts-defense.rationale: All within the state; security and justice are state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Militarism was strong and the Empire was to be defended by strength, with isolationist armed defence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Mosley opposed race-mixing and immigration but rejected Nazi racial laws as unsuitable for a multi-ethnic empire, so British nation more than a single ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Mosley held class war would be eliminated by permanent machinery of government and attacked Communists' "blood of class war".

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy, leadership and rejection of egalitarianism characterised the movement; outcomes were to reflect function and service.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; imperial outlook implies imperial rather than indigenous authority, though Mosley opposed imposing Western culture on empire peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Imperial pride and defence of the Empire as civilising heir to Rome make reparations unthinkable.

civilizational-union.rationale: Early rhetoric framed fascism as European, but Mosley insisted Britain lead and later pan-Europeanism (Union Movement) came postwar, so the strand is split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: "Liberty in private life. Obligation in public life." The doctrine put national duty above self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: "Obligation in public life" and "All within the State" place duty to the nation first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No relevant position in the sources.

limit-population.rationale: Pro-natalist and nationalist concerns, with eugenics in later strands, but no documented policy of limiting population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Mosley embraced rationalised industry and wanted an industrial civilisation under state direction.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Mosley embraced technology but wanted its effects controlled by the state rather than disruption of institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from discipline and eugenic traditions; the later NF favoured eugenics but not individual transhumanist freedom.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; technocratic government by experts but leader-led, so not handed to algorithms.

restore-past-order.rationale: Appeals to Tudors and medieval guilds mix with a modernist, forward-looking Greater Britain, so adherents are split between restoration and progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Mosley stressed action over committees and talk but also a defined ideology of the corporate state.

direct-action.rationale: Blackshirts used mass mobilisation, marches and stewarding, but also contested elections, so it favoured action beyond parliament without rejecting elections entirely.

means-match-ends.rationale: The BUF used violence and discipline to build an authoritarian state, though Mosley framed Fascism as continuous leadership.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The corporate state organised society by occupation and function.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Wages and profit remained, regulated by corporate bodies; need-based distribution is a communist idea.

production-for-use.rationale: Mosley wanted production tied to national consumption and purchasing power but kept enterprise and profit within limits.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Mosley allowed enterprise and profit and rejected the Marxist analysis of class war.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejected as Communist class war that would shed blood; classes cooperate in corporations.

collective-farming.rationale: Agriculture was to be saved by exclusion of foreign food and protection, with owners remaining.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Mosley blamed alien finance and the Parliamentary system for problems, not capitalism as such, and saw war as a means for national identity.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is supreme and finance serves it.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberty in private life but obligation in public life, and the state directs public life.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individuals are subordinated to the state and duty, not the holders of primary rights.

conscription.rationale: Militarism and national duty favour compulsory service, though not stressed in the sources opened.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The exit ideal of the individual is opposed by the totalising state.

state-as-business.rationale: The corporate state is a collective national organisation, not a customer-service model, though it admired efficient rationalised management.

positive-liberty.rationale: Mosley linked unemployment to weak purchasing power and wanted to guarantee economic security, but freedom was framed as duty and obligation.

media-academia-power.rationale: Antisemitic conspiracy views blamed Jewish finance and press; the specific university and media claim is a modest inference.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racialist views were common across British fascist groups, with Leese's league explicitly racial, though Mosley's mainstream was cultural.

organic-representation.rationale: The occupational franchise: "A steel worker will vote as a steel worker; a doctor as a doctor, a mother as a mother."

total-state.rationale: "All within the State; none outside the State; none against the State."

national-rebirth.rationale: Fascism as spiritual renewal of a declining Britain: "The spirit lives; the rest will follow."

territorial-expansion.rationale: Imperial pride but the BUF aimed to consolidate and defend the existing Empire, with selective pacifism, not conquer new territory.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Loyalty to the leader and the Crown was stressed but not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of the programme; wage-earners were organised in modern corporations.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: No stated position in the sources opened; the movement valued will and action but left no epistemology on power and truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Nationalist particularism, with religion respected but no universal rationalism documented.

single-common-good.rationale: Corporatism denies conflicting class interests and subordinates all to a national good set by the state.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The BUF turned antisemitic in 1934-36 and Mosley later blamed Jewish finance; Zionist statehood was not part of its programme.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporations were state-supervised bodies, not democratic votes of workers and public.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state direction of education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Mosley's 1930 memorandum was proto-Keynesian and he criticised deflation and credit restriction.

economic-freedom.rationale: Mosley rejected laissez-faire and put economic activity under the state.

rule-by-example.rationale: The leader and disciplined youth were to inspire by dedication, but laws and force were also used.

national-self-determination.rationale: Strongly nationalist and non-interventionist, though subordinating peoples of the Empire.

force-without-un.rationale: The BUF opposed wars except in defence of Britain or the Empire and disdained the League, so split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Mosley emphasised spirit, will and action over reason and talk.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: "Britain for the British" and the later National Front put citizens ahead of immigrants in welfare and housing.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not directly addressed; inferred from obligation in public life and corporate organisation of employment.

class-collaboration.rationale: Corporate machinery eliminates class war, with employers and employees partners in corporations.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Appeals to English tradition, the Tudors and medieval guilds oppose sacrificing heritage.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers were integrated into the national corporate state, not an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Women were educated to serve family and nation and married women's work was discouraged, though the BUF also supported equal pay and ending the marriage bar.

ban-interest.rationale: Finance was to serve industry rather than be abolished, though alien finance was attacked.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Mosley opposed race-mixing but rejected Nazi racial laws; the Leese strand and the NF later supported separation, so split.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state stands above classes and is the arbiter of all.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from autarky and industrial self-sufficiency.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The aim was fewer immigrants and no mixing, not assimilation; the NF later demanded repatriation.

elite-replacement.rationale: The later NF promoted a white genocide conspiracy but the interwar BUF did not, so the strands split.

proportional-representation.rationale: Party-based parliamentary representation was rejected in favour of an occupational franchise.

national-mission.rationale: Mosley insisted Britain should lead the world and the Empire as heir to Rome's civilising tradition, but did not propose spreading its political system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The movement upheld male-favoured wages and denied systemic male advantage as a problem.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Mosley attacked the Parliamentary system and old parties as obstructive, talk-driven and unable to act.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics were favoured by the National Front, but the opened BUF sources do not mention it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The movement valued the authority of security forces and Blackshirt discipline and rejected such accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The corporate state directs industry and life, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mosley opposed race-mixing, and the NF later also opposed interracial marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Racialist hierarchy and imperial paternalism contradict equal rights, though Mosley opposed imposing Western culture on empire peoples.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Autarky of nation and Empire is the aim, and Marxist internationalism is rejected.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The movement celebrated the British Empire and its settlement.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed by the interwar movement; with no religious-law minorities at issue, no position is documented and none is guessed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The BUF professed religious toleration, so conversion restrictions were not an aim.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No relevance for British fascism; not part of any programme.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The BUF opposed atheism and sought closer church-state links, so religious instruction in state schools would be supported.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Concerns the Soviet case; no relevant position for British fascism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mosley claimed leadership with popular consent ("By Dictatorship we mean Leadership") and said voters could remove governments, though other members rejected it.

trade-surplus.rationale: Exports were a surplus after the large home market was served.

population-transfer.rationale: The NF demanded compulsory repatriation of non-white people; interwar mainstream was less explicit, so only mild.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Blackshirts used force, and Mosley's "Power and Will" held forceful action necessary.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Militarist and imperial thought held struggle between peoples to be the expression of national identity, though economics were collectively organised.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The BUF opposed bans on itself, with the Public Order Act 1936 being resented, but it would outlaw Communists.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Individual liberty was subordinated to obligation, with state authority paramount.

separated-powers.rationale: Mosley wanted strong executive government and denounced Parliament's obstruction.

vanguard-party.rationale: Marxist concept; the BUF was a party-led mass movement but that was not described as proletarian vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The corporate state aimed at national interest, with attention to the unemployed but not poor-first priority.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing sales were not an issue in the 1930s programme, and nothing opened says how adherents would answer.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were to be replaced by corporate arbitration of wages, though secret ballots were not the method.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Mosley blamed overproduction against weak demand, not population, for unemployment.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Opposition to immigration and race-mixing rested on cohesion and the white standard of life.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Specialist elected chambers and leadership are the opposite.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Fascist rule invoked strong executive power against internal enemies like Communists, with the BUF defending the idea of strong government.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Corporations were to regulate wages and prices by permanent machinery.

party-controls-media.rationale: Totalitarian leanings and desire for an Italian or German dictatorship suggest it but opened sources do not state this.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Immigration and citizenship were to be restricted under "Britain for the British".

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No stated position; inferred as inconsistent with the specialist elite chamber.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Autarchy of nation and Empire; later Union Movement pan-Europeanism was postwar and a different strand.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Strong executive leadership and loyalty to the Crown; leader would command government, so mild yes.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Closer church-state ties were sought but nothing on church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religion was respected but the state, not clergy, was supreme.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Militarist and national-loyalty ethos opposes defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral renewal and opposition to permissiveness suggest it, but not stated in opened sources.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: A leader unconstrained by Parliament would hold power until removed, though Mosley said voters could remove governments.

recall-officials.rationale: Mosley said voters could still remove governments, but no explicit recall mechanism.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Isolationist foreign policy and non-interventionism from 1938 opposed entanglement, though Empire defence was sought.

people-in-arms.rationale: Militarism favoured regulated state armed forces, not a people's militia, though Blackshirts were paramilitary.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agriculture was to be saved by protection and exclusion of foreign food, and fascist rhetoric valued the countryside, but the BUF was an industrial modernist movement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The BUF's Northern Irish branch backed a united Ireland, but this was not a core principle.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Hostility to talkative political classes suggests it, but university specifics are not documented.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Imperial and racial hierarchy, with the Empire the heir of Rome's civilising tradition.

death-penalty.rationale: The NF favoured capital punishment; the interwar BUF law-and-order outlook suggests the same.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Moral conservatism and distinct gender roles oppose it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Opposition to permissiveness in the later NF and moral renewal themes.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: "Britain for the British" and the later NF's whites-only citizenship favour descent-based citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist unity opposes it.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; the state supreme over all.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Discipline, uniformity and obligation in public life oppose conformity-breaking, though private life was free.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; imperial and anti-reparation outlook.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Fascism would replace Parliament by corporate state, not a democratic assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: State authority and obligation in public life were justified by national economic renewal.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: National-first autarky with no foreign obligations.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from militarism and national independence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Crown was the symbol of imperial splendour, and the leader held power by movement leadership.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Finance must serve production and the state: "the handmaid of industry".

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Imperial territorial pride; inferred, no documented position.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property and profit were allowed only within national limits and under the state.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Saw the USSR mainly as the threat to the Empire; the specific theory is not documented.

collective-defense.rationale: Selective pacifism and non-interventionism rejected automatic commitments, such as the Polish guarantee.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The sources opened show no position on the legal status of annexed territory, so it is left neutral rather than inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: A closer church-state link was sought, but the state over Church and Church support are in tension.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The monarchy as a symbol of imperial splendour standing above party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Imperial unity; the Empire was to be held together, with the BUF's strong nationalism.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Loyalty to the Crown but no divine descent doctrine.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; opposed as inconsistent with corporate direction of the economy.

character-from-environment.rationale: Racialist and hereditarian thought (Leese) favours innate nature, with discipline also stressed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The corporate state with a strong executive is not a balance of the few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Mosley was a charismatic leader and the BUF used uniforms, mass rallies and the leader principle.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Socialism was rejected, and class war was to be eliminated by corporate machinery.

land-redistribution.rationale: Property would be kept within the state, with no breakup of estates.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened; no documented stance on refugees or descendants returning, so neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Interwar BUF stressed the British Empire not co-ethnic claims.

women-must-cover.rationale: Nothing in the programme suggests this, and BUF courted women.

common-currency.rationale: Autarchy of nation and Empire with sovereign national finance; opposed to pooled European monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Mosley insisted Britain lead and later Union Movement pan-Europeanism was postwar and not the interwar mainstream.

decide-locally.rationale: Mosley wanted strong executive government and a unitary corporate state, with Parliament's committees and divided authority rejected.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The BUF was a disciplined, uniformed, leader-led movement in which members followed the leader's decisions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Mosley's leader was to bypass legal obstruction and Parliament, though he insisted on popular consent, so only a hedged inference.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Mosley's stated aim was autarchy, the self-contained Nation and Empire, with conditional protection and exclusion of foreign food.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: the BUF wanted one organic nation and Empire under the state and was hostile to minorities, so self-governing minority institutions had no place.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred: the movement's antisemitism and anti-immigrant stance rejected minority equality; Leese's strand wanted Jews removed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Fascism is described in the scholarship as rejecting Marxist materialism in favour of national rebirth, will and duty, which Mosley's programme reflects.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred: the corporate state organised each industry into a state-supervised body of employers and workers rather than enforcing competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred: Mosley wanted the state to direct finance and industry for national ends, so rescuing national industry was consistent with the programme.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: Mosley wanted a government with power to act without obstruction from parliamentary or other checks; the model was leader-led, not majority-led, so agreement is weak.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The BUF's occupational franchise and policy on women stressed women's role as mothers and rejected equal-quota representation.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: Mosley preferred protection and an economically self-contained Empire to international trade rules.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: the movement called for duty, service and sacrifice to the nation, but kept wages and the corporate system.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred: fascism exalted action and the Blackshirts used force, but the BUF sought power through politics and was restricted by the Public Order Act 1936.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The BUF professed loyalty to the monarchy and kept hereditary institutions as part of national order.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Mosley's fascism was ultranationalist and imperial, centring the Nation and Empire as the object of loyalty.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Greater Britain defended British rule of the Empire, and Mosley's plans treated colonial peoples as wards of a superior power.

patriotic-education.rationale: The BUF demanded a youth moulded to serve the nation, with national loyalty as the first aim of schooling.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: the movement was racially nationalist and would not favour minority preferences, though the question is anachronistic.

public-money-creation.rationale: Mosley's plan subordinated finance to the state and proposed state control of credit, though he did not demand abolition of bank lending.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Fascists claimed the corporate state would rescue capitalism from crisis, so adaptation is possible; inferred from that claim.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from the movement's imperialism: it wanted Britain to keep and develop its Empire; the statement itself is about a former empire.

delink-world-market.rationale: Mosley wanted an Empire bloc shielded from outside trade, but the statement concerns poor countries delinking, and the movement had no stance on it.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: fascism rejected class-struggle analysis and held that workers and employers share a national interest.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Mixed: the movement was racist and favoured discrimination but also subordinated private property to the state.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Fascism rejected limits on the state and replaced parliamentary government with strong leadership and the corporate state.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Fascists defended the Empire and its settlements; inferred from the Nation-and-Empire programme, not a stated view on treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: The BUF kept the monarchy and sought a mandated leader and corporate state, not an elected head of state; inferred from its constitutional proposals.

minority-veto.rationale: The leader principle and rule by a strong government override dissent; the corporate state gave no veto to minorities.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Mosley stressed duty and obedience to the state and its leader; resistance to a lawful ruler is inferred to be unwelcome.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The BUF aimed to replace party-political Parliament with an occupationally elected body under a government with wide powers, so Parliament was not to be supreme.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animals were not a theme in Mosley's programme; left neutral.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a conventional pro-agriculture, pro-farming stance of the period.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Class collaboration and duty to the nation implied obligations of the privileged; inferred from the corporate-state ethic of service.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Fascism demanded active service, action and national rebirth, the opposite of withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Fascists attacked decadent culture and press, but as corrupting the nation rather than pacifying the masses; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Mosley held that the old parties served finance and were to be replaced by authority and dynamism; consent-through-culture is not his framing.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Hostility to alien finance and a belief in an economically self-contained Empire imply that outside capital drains the nation; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Hostility to immigrants and race-mixing implies favouring natives for office; inferred, not stated.

party-own-road.rationale: Concerns communist and socialist parties; fascists favoured national roads for every nation but opposed socialism, so neutral.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Autarchy, the self-contained Nation and Empire, was a stated aim of the BUF.

return-lost-territory.rationale: No stated position on lost territory; the BUF was non-interventionist from 1938.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Imperial fascism and racial hierarchy put the Empire's British rulers over native peoples; inferred from its imperial and racial stance.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascism is by definition opposed to anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The BUF opposed Communism and presented fascism as a legitimate order, so it rejected the equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The BUF did not address the American Civil War; left neutral.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Nationalist traditionalism favours preserving national heritage; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; the BUF's gender policy stressed distinct roles for women.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened; left neutral as no position can be inferred from the ideology's principles.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Fascists rejected liberal parliamentarism as unfit for the modern age and wanted a corporate state; inferred as a general claim.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Mosley wanted a disciplined nation led by authority, with the services loyal to the state; inferred for the guardian role.

paid-care-work.rationale: The BUF wanted women organised as mothers within the corporate franchise; recognition of mothers' work is inferred, payment is not stated.

filial-duty.rationale: Fascism promoted traditional family and national duty, but filial obligation was not a documented plank; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Fascism put authority in the leader and a corporate state with occupational representation, not in examined officials; it also claimed to scorn party patronage.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Mosley wanted a self-contained national and imperial economy shut off from outside finance and goods, which implies blocking foreign control of firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Fascism glorified the family and national rebirth and is inferred to oppose easy divorce; not a documented plank.

recallable-delegates.rationale: British fascism rejected parliamentary and party democracy in favor of a strong leader, and an instructed recallable delegate system runs against that.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The corporate state put economic life under state direction, so private individual accounts are inferred to be disfavored; not documented.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The corporate state accepted private property under state direction and national interest; communal land tenure is inferred to be rejected.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Mosley sought to replace Parliament with a government empowered to act without party-political obstruction, including on finance.

single-official-language.rationale: Ultranationalist movements favored a unified national culture; inferred, as language was not a documented issue in Britain.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Its protection of national and imperial economic self-sufficiency and hostility to alien finance imply barring foreign land ownership; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The movement opposed immigration and held race-based views, so it rejected any outcome-based anti-discrimination doctrine.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Fascist rhetoric spoke of national discipline and sacrifice, but Mosley also promised higher consumption through high wages; split, inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Mosley's program favored peace unless British territory or empire was attacked, and so opposed entanglement abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Its peacetime non-interventionism and imperial focus make it inferred to reject force within an alliance; no direct statement.

corporate-influence.rationale: Mosley blamed parliament's subjection to finance and vested interests and wanted industry subordinated to the nation, which implies agreement though he did not target corporate lobbying specifically.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from his autarchic, nationalist stance and rejection of alien finance; no statement on NGO or media funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the BUF's national-rebirth rhetoric, its emphasis on women's role as mothers and its hostility to immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: The corporate state was centralised under national authority, so local bodies limiting property purchases would cut across it.

job-guarantee.rationale: Mosley's programme was to end unemployment by organising production and purchasing power through the state and corporations, with work for all as the aim.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: it rejected parliamentary democracy as decadent, and the BUF saw democracy-spreading as no route to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Duty to the state and discipline are central to Mosley's creed, and he subordinated the individual to the nation.

non-intervention.rationale: The BUF campaigned for non-intervention in foreign wars from 1938 ('Mind Britain's Business'), while still holding empire as Britain's own sphere.

industrial-unions.rationale: The corporate system organised employers and workers by industry under state authority, though independent unions were to be replaced.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The BUF's antisemitism grew through the 1930s, portraying Jews and alien finance as hostile to Britain, and was central to Leese's Imperial Fascist League.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Fascism held the family and motherhood central to national rebirth, so dissolving legal marriage is opposed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: the authoritarian, leader-centred state gave no weight to open records, and the BUF backed the Public Order Act-era secrecy of the movement.

local-production.rationale: The aim was a self-contained Nation and Empire, which is national or imperial rather than local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: The BUF was a disciplined, uniformed, hierarchical organisation under the Leader, the opposite of small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Mosley held that the sovereign nation should answer to no external authority, and the BUF opposed the League of Nations.

religious-nation.rationale: The BUF defined the nation by race and loyalty to Britain and Empire, not by shared religion, though it accepted Christian forms.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from its imperial nationalism: it rejected subordination to other powers, though it did not discuss ritual tribute.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from its centralised corporate state and imperial economic bloc, which pooled national resources under state direction rather than regional retention.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The corporate state kept private property and enterprise under state authority, not common ownership of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Hostility to Communism was a core platform of the BUF and the wider fascist movement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: the corporate system organised industries under state authority while retaining private enterprise, so private delivery within a state-led framework fits.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from its national-rebirth and spiritual-duty language; religion was treated as a lasting national element, not an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: Mosley presented the old capitalist and finance-led order as outdated and decadent, to be replaced by the corporate state.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The BUF held a domestic role for women and sought change by corporatism, not by economic transformation for gender equality.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on women as mothers and family duty, which favors private home and child care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: no source opened shows a program to purge loanwords; the movement was nationalist but did not make language purity an issue.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from its view that national authority outranks other arrangements; it left no position on treaties with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: It wanted a unitary nation and Empire organised by the corporate state, the opposite of small self-governing communes holding property in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its imperial and racial nationalism, which favored settling British people within the Empire; no direct source on minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Mosley presented the corporate state as a third course beyond both liberal capitalism and Marxist socialism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Fascists stressed national and imperial rebirth, but no source records a view on historical land claims; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mosley's BUF was antisemitic but the mainstream strand denied it after the war; Holocaust denial arose in postwar heirs, not in the BUF's own period.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The BUF's period treated morals as secondary and the postwar National Front is the strand that states stances on sexuality; inferred as neutral.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The BUF aimed to replace party politics with a single leader and corporate state and used the Public Order Act context to attack rivals.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: British fascism claimed to defend Christian civilisation but largely gave no priority to blasphemy law; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Greater Britain sought an economically self-contained Empire in which the colonies served the home country's industry.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The strand was anti-Muslim imperial in outlook and had no doctrine of Muslim resistance; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: British fascism supported the monarchy and existing state authority; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The occupational franchise and leader-led corporate state replaced direct local participation with hierarchical state authority.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The strand held racial, imperial and class-harmony ideas that deny oppression as a frame.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Interwar fascism held traditional gender roles and later heirs oppose such recognition; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: British fascism spoke of national vitality and eugenics, but no source gives a position on assisted dying; split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Mosley held that fascism went beyond left and right in a national movement of service, combining state direction and private enterprise.

alienated-labor.rationale: The corporate state rejected class war between worker and employer and Marxist critique; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Postwar heirs are hostile to Islam, but the interwar BUF predates large Muslim migration; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: British fascism claimed national rather than divine authority, though it kept the monarchy and church; split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: No source records a view on religious dress in state institutions; inferred neutral.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The corporate state subordinated individual employees' rights to national and industrial discipline; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: The corporate state aimed at state-organised cooperation of capital and labour, not social-market or laissez-faire models; split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The BUF stressed national strength and the military, so abolishing armed forces is contrary to its aims.

rich-first.rationale: The corporate state emphasised national solidarity and planned industry, opposing letting some groups get rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: From 1938 the BUF campaigned for peace and non-intervention, with Mosley's Mind Britain's Business slogan, keeping Britain out of continental alliances.

missingStatements.text: Parliament should be replaced by a body elected by occupation rather than by geographic constituency.
missingStatements.rationale: Mosley's occupational franchise, where a steel worker votes as a steel worker and a mother as a mother, was central to the corporate state.

missingStatements.text: A country and its colonies should form a self-sufficient economic bloc shut off from outside trade.
missingStatements.rationale: Mosley's stated aim was autarchy, the self-contained Nation and Empire, with conditional protection and exclusion of foreign food.

missingStatements.text: Finance should be subordinated to productive industry and national purposes.
missingStatements.rationale: Mosley called finance the handmaid of industry and aimed to direct British finance to equip British industry, attacking alien finance.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to interwar corporatist economics; the positions on regulating corporations and finance are already carried by regulate-corporations, ban-interest and corporatist-bargaining.

missingStatements.text: In peacetime a country should avoid wars unless its own territory or empire is under attack.
missingStatements.rationale: The BUF practised selective pacifism, opposing wars except in defence of Britain or the Empire, and opposed the guarantee to Poland.
missingStatements.declined: Covered loosely by military-superiority, force-without-un and war-builds-character; a conditional pacifism too specific to the BUF to add.

notes: The Mosley BUF mainstream was in its own terms cultural and imperial rather than biologically racial, rejected Nazi racial laws and supported loyalty to the Crown; Leese's Imperial Fascist League and the later National Front were openly racial, antisemitic and pro-Nazi, and would answer race, antisemitism, eugenics and repatriation statements more strongly. Mosley's women's policies (equal pay, ending the marriage bar) coexisted with distinct gender roles. Several answers on modern issues are low-confidence inferences.
